text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Some 400 Bulgarian towns and villages were left without electricity after heavy snowstorms on Thursday, the Civil Defence Service said.

-- The Socialist parliamentary group is expected to discuss proposals for a new premier today after Zhan Videnov submitted the resignation of the cabinet at an extraordinary party congress on Saturday.
-- Sales of new cars have fallen by 30 percent in 1996 in comparison with the previous year, the chairman of the Car Importers' Union Boris Marekov said.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to discuss on Saturday the sale of a stake in the state United Bulgarian Bank to the European Bank for Investment and Development, deputy prime minister Roumen Gechev said.
-- Bulgaria's parliament is expected to vote the resignation of Zhan Videnov's cabinet at an extraordinary session on Saturday.
-- The chairman of the socialist parliamentary group Krasimir Premyanov submitted his resignation following the party congress, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
-- Bulgaria's Himko Vratsa chemical plant is expected to post some 9.7 billion levs profit for 1996, its executive director Kiril Petkov said.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet discussed at an extraordinary meeting on Tuesday a 1997 draft budget pegging the lev at 500 per dollar and envisaging 72 percent annual inflation, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank appealed to the Supreme Court against a ruling by the Sofia City Court rejecting its insolvency suit against First Private Bank.
-- A hand grenade exploded in the yard of the Yugoslav consulate in Sofia early on Wednesday but no victims or serious damage were reported, the interior ministry said.
